Rain Dance (Japanese: あまごい Rain Prayer) is a non-damaging Water-type move introduced in Generation II.

It is:

  • TM18 from Generation II to Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon, and in Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl.
  • TM33 in Pokémon Sword and Shield.
  • TM050 in Generation IX.

Effect

Generation II

When this move is used, a rainfall will start on the field which will last for five turns. This clears any other weather and it's possible to use it even if it is already raining.

While Rain Dance is in effect, the base damage of Water-type moves will be increased by 50%, whereas the base damage of Solar Beam and Fire-type moves will be decreased by 50%. Additionally, Synthesis, Morning Sun, and Moonlight will recover only half as much HP as under clear conditions. Thunder ignores accuracy and evasion under the effect of Rain Dance.

Generation III to VIII

If a Damp Rock is held when Rain Dance is used, the duration of rainfall is lengthened from 5 to 8 turns. Rain Dance will fail if it's already raining. Hurricane ignores accuracy and evasion under the effect of Rain Dance. In Diamond and Pearl only, the move Thunder has a 30% chance of bypassing Protect and Detect under Rain Dance.

A Pokémon with Rain Dish will restore 1/16 its maximum HP to itself after every turn, with Swift Swim will be twice as fast in the rain, with the Dry Skin Ability will regain ⅛ of their maximum HP at the end of each turn, and with Hydration will have their existing status conditions cured at the end of each turn. Moonlight, Synthesis and Morning Sun only restore ¼ of the user's maximum HP.

Additionally, Pokémon with Forecast transform into the Water type and Weather Ball becomes a Water-type move.

Rain Dance can be used as the first move of a Pokémon Contest combination, causing Bubble, BubbleBeam, Clamp, Crabhammer, Dive, Hydro Cannon, Hydro Pump, Muddy Water, Octazooka, Surf, Thunder, Water Gun, Water Pulse, Water Sport, Water Spout, Waterfall, Weather Ball, Whirlpool, and Withdraw to score double the normal appeal if used in the next turn. It is also part of a Contest Spectacular combination, causing certain moves (Hurricane, Soak, Thunder, Water Sport and Weather Ball) to give an extra three appeal points if used in the next turn.

Rain called by Rain Dance does not allow Sliggoo to evolve into Goodra.

If heavy rain, extremely harsh sunlight, or strong winds are present, Rain Dance will fail.

If powered up by a Waterium Z into Z-Rain Dance, the user's Speed stat is raised by one stage.

Generation IX

Rain Dance can no longer override weather in the overworld.

In other games

Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series

In Red Rescue Team and Blue Rescue Team, Rain Dance is a move with 12 PP. It turns the current floor's weather to rainy for 18 turns. This move is affected by Taunt.

In Explorers of Time, Darkness and Sky, the weather will not end unless changed or the player has moved to the next floor.

Description

Games Description
MDRB Changes the dungeon floor's weather to Rain over several turns.
MDTDS Changes the floor's weather to a Rain condition.
BSL フロアのてんきを 『あめ』にかえる
MDGtI It changes the floor's weather to a Rain condition. Under a Rain condition, the power of Fire-type moves goes down, and the power of Water-type moves goes up.
SMD It changes the floor's weather to rain. During rain, the power of Fire-type moves goes down and the power of Water-type moves goes up.


In the anime

Main series

Lugia Gyarados The clouds Dragonair
The user summons dark clouds from overhead, causing rain to fall.
Pokémon Method
User First Used In Notes
Slowpoke Slowpoke yawns, causing clouds to appear in the sky.
Multiple wild Slowpoke A Shadow of a Drought Debut
Lugia Lugia's body becomes surrounded in a crimson red aura, making a storm appear.
Lugia (anime) A Parent Trapped! None
Dragonair The orb on Dragonair's neck or Dragonair's body shines brightly and storm clouds appear, making it rain.
Clair's Dragonair Great Bowls of Fire! None
Alakazam Alakazam crosses its spoons and a light blue energy ball forms in front of them. It then shoots the energy ball into the sky, creating storm clouds and making it rain.
Vito Winstrate's Alakazam Candid Camerupt! None
Dusclops Dusclops dances around, always staying on one leg and switching back and forth between the two. It also moves its hands back and forth first with its palms open, then with its index fingers sticking up. After a while, rain clouds appear in the sky and it starts to pour.
A wild Dusclops Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None
Koffing Koffing moves and spins its body around. After a while, rain clouds appear in the sky and it starts to pour.
A wild Koffing Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None
Gengar Gengar does a hula-like dance, then sticks its backside in the air and shakes it around. After a while, dark rain clouds appear and it starts to pour.
A wild Gengar Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None
Haunter Haunter dances around by clawing the air back and forth. After a while, dark rain clouds appear and it starts to pour.
A wild Haunter Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None

A wild Shuppet Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None
Gastly Gastly dances by floating back and forth. After a while, dark rain clouds appear and it starts to pour.
A wild Gastly Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None
Misdreavus Misdreaves dances by floating back and forth and occasionally spinning its body around in the air. After a while, dark rain clouds appear and it starts to pour.
A wild Misdreavus Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None
Duskull Duskull dances by crouching with its hands over its eye, then opening them and shaking its body. After a while, dark rain clouds appear and it starts to pour.
A wild Duskull Pikachu's Ghost Carnival None
Blastoise Blastoise fires two orbs of water from its hydro cannons into the sky at the sun. Then, rain clouds appear and it starts to rain; or, Blastoise summons a dark circular cloud that spins counterclockwise, with a dark indent in the middle of the cloud and then rain falls from the cloud.
Three Blastoise Kellyn captured with his Capture Styler Pokémon Ranger and the Kidnapped Riolu! Part 2 None
Tierno's Blastoise Valuable Experience for All! None

A wild Yamask A Night in the Nacrene City Museum! None

Tierno's Ludicolo Valuable Experience for All! None
A wild Ludicolo Up to Your Neck! None

Clemont's Magneton Battling with a Clean Slate! None

Misty's Gyarados When Regions Collide! None

Trivia

  • This move was Blastoise's Pokémon Power (as あまごい / Rain Prayer in Japanese and as Rain Dance in English) in the Base Set of the TCG prior to being introduced in Generation II of the games.
  • In Generation II, Rain Dance was the only Water-type move that could be taught via TM.
  • In Generation III, Rain Dance starts a Contest combination with 19 possible finishing moves, the most of any combination
  • Prior to Generation VIII, Bronzong was the only Pokémon able to learn Rain Dance by leveling up that could not learn any moves or have any Abilities that benefited from rain. This may be related to its Pokédex entries, several of which mention Bronzong's natural power to summon rain clouds. With the addition of Weather Ball to its movepool in Generation VIII, this is no longer the case.
  • The original Japanese name of this move is unrelated to dancing, therefore this is not a dance move. As such, Rain Dance is unaffected by Dancer, and Tierno does not request to see a Pokémon with this move in Pokémon X and Y.
    • Even if it were a dance move, it would fail if called via Dancer, as Rain Dance fails if it's already raining.
  • Rain Dance is based off amagoi, Shinto prayer and rituals for rain. Its English name comes from the fact that some of its varieties include dance rituals.
